short: Lip-timed phonemes into a codec LM (M06) are standard; Chem WER edges EmoDubber 12.5% vs 12.8%, no SyncNet scores, and the stated sync gains do not follow from Table 1.
position: VSpeechLM [@wang2025vspeechlm] changes one component, synthesis (M06): a per-frame phoneme aligner feeds a pretrained codec language model instead of a duration-based, diffusion or flow decoder. Both halves are standard: lip-set phoneme durations without a duration predictor appear in Hegde et al. [@hegde2023towards] (§3.2.2), and the authors cite an earlier speech-LLM dubbing system, DubWise, with global duration control only (§1). The content gain over the strongest baseline is small, 12.5% against 12.8% WER on Chem (Table 1); the baseline value is the non-ground-truth-reference row of the [concurrent] DiFlowDubber, which reports 11.12% against 12.81% in the same setting [@nguyen2026diflowdubber]. The synchronization claim is the weakest: it rests on a length-weighted spectral distance (§4.1), and its headline reductions do not follow from Table 1. The evaluation (M12) omits the SyncNet scores that DiFlowDubber's tables give for six earlier dubbing systems, four of them this paper's baselines.
